summary.what_changed: Reworked the `commands` criterion in the CLAUDE.md health auditor (`scripts/claude-md-audit.mjs`). It previously scored 7 points per fenced code block containing a recognized tool keyword, which rewarded fragmenting commands into many small blocks and ignored commands documented in linked `.md` files. The new `countCommandLines()` counts actual executable command lines inside fences (stripping `$ ` prompts, skipping blanks/comments), and `extractDocRefs`/`resolveLinkedCommands` follow backticked-path, markdown-link, and `@import` references to linked docs (bounded to the target root, `.md` only, max 25 files, 256 KB each) and credit their command lines at half weight (capped at 10 of the 20 possible points). The recognized tool-token list was also broadened to cover Python-first tooling (`uv`, `pytest`, `ruff`, `mypy`, `alembic`, `prefect`) alongside existing tokens. `scoreFile()` gains an optional 4th `opts.linkedCommandLines` parameter (default 0); all existing 3-arg call sites are unaffected.
summary.why: A real CLAUDE.md audited at 7/20 on the commands criterion despite thoroughly documenting build/test/run commands, because it consolidated commands into one well-organized fenced block (penalizing consolidation) and referenced 23 linked `.md` docs containing the actual command lines, none of which the auditor read. The criterion was measuring a proxy (fence count) instead of the property it claims to score (does this file tell an agent how to build/test/run), and unrecognized Python tooling made the problem worse for non-JS repos. The fix realigns the metric with intent and was calibrated against the real file (83/B → 96/A, commands 7/20 → 20/20).

doc_targets.notes: Documents the new countCommandLines/extractDocRefs/resolveLinkedCommands scoring mechanism and the `commands = min(20, ownLines*4 + min(10, linkedLines*2))` formula so the audit tool's behavior is discoverable outside the source diff and design spec. summary.what_changed: Fixed the session-kind classifier (`classifySessionKind` in `scripts/_usage-data.mjs`) to fail closed on unrecognized transcript entrypoints. Previously it enumerated known SDK entrypoints and let anything else fall through to `unknown`, which is admitted by the `interactive_or_unknown` posture universe used by Memory & Terminal Execution scoring. An unhandled `sdk-py` entrypoint plus a 5-line scan bound (too shallow for transcripts that lead with `queue-operation`/`attachment` rows) caused 265 of 612 in-window sessions (43%) to misclassify as `unknown`, diluting the Memory Execution denominator to 353 against a true 93 (3.8x) and scoring a well-instrumented machine at 37/100. The fix inverts the classifier to an allow-list (`INTERACTIVE_ENTRYPOINTS = {cli, claude-desktop}`) so every other entrypoint resolves to `observer` or `sdk_orchestrated` instead of `unknown`, and raises the scan bound to `ENTRYPOINT_SCAN_BOUND = 200`.
summary.why: Root cause was a classifier that failed open instead of closed: unknown/unhandled entrypoints and an undersized scan window silently entered a posture-scoring denominator meant to represent only user-driven interactive sessions, producing a severely understated Memory Execution score. Fixing this restores denominator integrity (93 true interactive-or-unknown sessions vs. the inflated 353) and moved Memory Execution 37↚100 and overall Execution 60↚68 on the measured machine.

summary.what_changed: Added three new rules to the project's CLAUDE.md memory file, each distilled from a specific incident during the CCE-170/171/172/173 work cycle: (1) before removing accidental persistence of a file, check whether anything depends on it as a side-channel data source, since a file committed by mistake can still be someone's only durable record; (2) detection code shipped in place of a withdrawn fix must state, in the same PR, both the threshold that reopens the fix and the date at which zero findings means deleting the detector; (3) a probe reading a nonexistent schema key silently returns a zero indistinguishable from a real zero, so any reported absence should be accompanied by a positive control proving the measurement channel works. No code changed; only CLAUDE.md.
summary.why: Each rule came from something that cost real time during the cycle rather than from a general principle. CCE-170 (PR #265 in engineering-docs-agent) correctly removed a committed data file, but that file's git history turned out to be the only durable archive of CCE-141 diagnostic firings that CCE-172 depends on, revealing an invisible side-effect dependency. CCE-141's detection-only diagnostic, shipped with no exit criterion, sat for three weeks across four hosts with zero recorded findings before anyone could answer whether there was data yet. And a mid-session probe for a nonexistent `pages_authored` field returned a plausible-looking zero that only became distinguishable from a broken measurement once a genuine positive-control field was found in the same snapshots.
